summary.text: A peptide bond is a covalent bond of the amide type that links two consecutive alpha-amino acids along a peptide or protein chain.
It forms in a condensation reaction in which the two joined amino acids give off one molecule of water.
Forming it consumes energy, which in organisms comes from ATP, and once formed it is extremely slow to break by water alone.

facts.label: Byproduct of joining
facts.value: One molecule of water per bond

facts.label: Energy source
facts.value: ATP supplies the energy to form it

items.prompt: Two amino acids join into a dipeptide. The reaction also gives off a small molecule. Which one?

options.label: Carbon dioxide
Water
Ammonia
Oxygen gas

items.explain: The reaction produces one molecule of water as well as two amino acids joined by a peptide bond.

items.prompt: Joining amino acids into a chain uses up energy. In living things, what supplies it?

options.label: ATP
The water given off
Sunlight on the bond
Heat from the surroundings

items.explain: Forming the peptide bond consumes energy, which in organisms is derived from ATP.

items.prompt: A peptide bond has partial double-bond character. What does that do to the group?

options.label: It lets the group spin freely like a hinge
It bends the group into a pyramid
It splits the group into two charged halves
It holds the group flat in one plane

items.explain: The partial double bond renders the amide group planar.

items.prompt: Digestion has to split peptide bonds quickly, yet water alone barely does it. What do living things normally use?

options.label: Ribosomes, the same machines that make proteins
More ATP, the same fuel that builds the bond
Enzymes called peptidases or proteases
Ultraviolet light from the sun

items.explain: Breaking the bond by water is extremely slow, and in living organisms it is normally catalyzed by peptidases or proteases.

items.prompt: Most peptide bonds overwhelmingly prefer one of two shapes, but those next to proline are far less lopsided. What is thought to explain this?

options.label: Proline bonds are broken by water far faster
Symmetry makes the two shapes nearly equal in energy
Proline bonds cannot rotate even slowly
Proline carries extra ATP energy

items.explain: The symmetry between two of proline’s atoms is thought to make the cis and trans forms nearly equal in energy.

items.prompt: Proteins usually fold in milliseconds, yet one folds far more slowly. What about its peptide groups could explain the delay?

options.label: Some sit in the nonnative form until they flip
They have all been split by hydrolysis
They have all gained a charge
They are too symmetric to ever isomerize

items.explain: A nonnative isomer of some peptide groups can disrupt folding, slowing or preventing it until the native isomer is reached.
